en.name: Sobrasada
en.summary: Sobrasada is a Mallorcan cured sausage soft enough to spread — pork, a great deal of fat and a great deal of paprika, matured in a casing. A whole uncut piece hangs for 2–3 months; cut, it keeps 2–3 weeks refrigerated, and 1–2 months frozen. The numbers are read across from sliced hard dry sausage rather than published for sobrasada.
en.pantry: A whole uncut sobrasada in its casing hangs in a cool, dry, ventilated place for about 2–3 months, which is how it is made and matured on Mallorca. It stays soft and spreadable because of the fat, not because it is underdone — the cure and the paprika do the work. Keep it below about 20 °C; in a warm kitchen the fat weeps out and the surface goes rancid. This is the least certain figure on the page, because sobrasada is far moister and fattier than the hard salami the number came from, so lean on your nose. If yours came chilled in a tub rather than in a casing, treat it as a refrigerated product from the start.
en.fridge: Once cut, refrigerate at 4 °C (40 °F) or below with the cut face covered, and use it within 2–3 weeks. Cold sobrasada is stiff, so cut what you need and let it warm before spreading, or melt it straight onto hot bread. A darkened, dried skin on the cut face can be scraped back and the paste underneath is fine; a sour or solvent-like smell means the fat has gone and nothing brings it back.
en.freezer: It freezes for 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and it freezes badly. The emulsion breaks, so what thaws is greasy and grainy — fine stirred into a stew or a rice dish, poor on toast. Freeze it in small portions wrapped tight, and accept that you are storing an ingredient rather than a spread. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; these months are a quality call.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, still wrapped, and use within a few days. Never on the counter, and do not refreeze.
spoilage: A sour or solvent-like smell from the fat, the usual way sobrasada ends.
Fuzzy green, grey or black mould as distinct from a dry white bloom on the casing.
Fat that has wept out and pooled, leaving the paste dry and separated.
The paste gone brown all through rather than only a thin skin on the cut face.
tips: Hang a whole one with air around it, well away from the stove.
Cover the cut face; a drying skin costs you the top layer every time.
Spread it on hot toast so the fat melts rather than fighting cold paste.
Buy the small sausages if you eat it slowly — cut, the clock is weeks not months.

faq.q: Does sobrasada need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: A whole uncut piece in a casing does not — hang it somewhere cool, dry and airy. Once cut, or if it came chilled in a tub, refrigerate it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: How long does sobrasada keep once cut?
faq.a: About 2–3 weeks refrigerated with the cut face covered. That figure is borrowed from sliced hard dry sausage.
For 1–2 months, but the emulsion breaks and it thaws greasy and grainy. Use it in cooking rather than on toast.

zh.name: 馬約卡可塗抹香腸
zh.summary: Sobrasada 是馬約卡島的熟成香腸，軟到可以直接塗——豬肉、大量油脂和大量紅椒粉，灌進腸衣熟成。完整未切開的整條可吊掛 2～3 個月；切開後冷藏 2～3 週，冷凍 1～2 個月。這些數字是比照「硬式乾香腸切片」讀來的，不是專為 sobrasada 公布的。
zh.pantry: 完整未切開、還在腸衣裡的 sobrasada，吊在陰涼、乾燥、通風處約 2～3 個月，馬約卡就是這樣做、這樣熟成的。它之所以軟到能塗，是因為油脂多，不是因為沒做熟——熟成與紅椒粉才是在工作的那兩樣。請保持在大約 20 °C 以下；廚房一熱，油脂就會滲出來，表面走油耗。這是本頁最不確定的一個數字，因為 sobrasada 比借數字給它的硬式莎樂美腸濕得多、也肥得多，所以請多靠鼻子判斷。如果你買到的是冷藏盒裝而不是整條腸衣款，就從一開始把它當冷藏品。
zh.fridge: 切開後放 4 °C 以下、切面蓋好，2～3 週內用完。冰過的 sobrasada 很硬，所以要吃多少切多少，回溫再塗，或者直接抹在熱吐司上讓它化開。切面若結了一層變深的乾皮，可以刮掉，下面的肉醬沒問題；但如果聞起來發酸或有溶劑味，就是油脂壞了，救不回來。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下可放 1～2 個月，而且凍得不太好。乳化會被破壞，解凍後又油又沙——丟進燉菜或燉飯沒問題，抹吐司就很差。請小份包緊冷凍，並接受你保存的是一種「食材」而不是抹醬。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，這裡的月數是品質判斷。
zh.thawing: 維持包裝放冷藏解凍，幾天內用完。不要放室溫，也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 油脂散發酸味或溶劑味，這是 sobrasada 最常見的結局。
長出綠、灰、黑色絨毛霉（腸衣上乾燥的白粉霜則正常）。
油脂滲出積成一灘，剩下的肉醬乾裂分離。
肉醬整體轉褐，而不只是切面那一層薄皮。
tips: 整條要吊起來讓四周通風，並且遠離爐火。
切面一定要蓋好；每次結乾皮就等於損失最上面一層。
抹在熱吐司上讓油脂化開，不要硬塗冰冷的肉醬。
吃得慢就買小條的——切開之後是以週計，不是以月計。

faq.a: 完整未切開、有腸衣的整條不需要，吊在陰涼乾燥通風處即可。切開之後，或本來就是冷藏盒裝的，就要放 4 °C 以下。

faq.q: sobrasada 切開後可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏、切面蓋好，約 2～3 週。這個數字借自硬式乾香腸切片。
可以放 1～2 個月，但乳化會被破壞，解凍後又油又沙。建議拿去入菜，不要抹麵包。
